 Navigating open enrollment: Louisiana Blue offers tips on making informed health insurance decisions for 2027
 BY AMANDA MCELFRESH | BRANDED CONTENT SPECIALIST 
 Amanda McElfresh

 This article is brought to you by Louisiana Blue. 
 With health insurance enrollment periods and deadlines nearing, now is an ideal time for people to evaluate their coverage and make decisions for 2027.
 Mike Bertaut, a healthcare economist with Louisiana Blue, said choosing the right plan involves more than comparing monthly premiums. From provider networks and prescription coverage to changes in federal financial assistance, understanding the details of each plan choice/option can help people avoid unexpected expenses.
 Here, Bertaut shares more advice on navigating open enrollment and finding coverage that meets individual medical needs and household budgets.
 What are the main health insurance options?  There are four ways to get covered: Medicare, Medicaid, employer coverage or a plan on HealthCare.gov .
 If you are employed, your first stop should be with your company’s HR department. Most employers subsidize health insurance plans for their employees at a better rate than HealthCare.gov . If you are not working or are a dependent on someone else’s plan, you may be eligible for Medicaid. In Louisiana, many parents have their own health insurance through their jobs, but their children are eligible for Medicaid. If you are 65 or older, or you have certain health conditions or disabilities, you may qualify for Medicare.
 Why is now the time to think about health insurance?  Many employers have open enrollment for next year’s insurance coverage during the last couple months of the year. In addition, individuals can start enrolling on HealthCare.gov on Nov. 1. If you want to be covered on Jan. 1, you need to choose a HealthCare.gov plan by Dec. 15.
 The annual enrollment period for Medicare is Oct. 15 to Dec. 7. That is the no-harm, no-foul period to change Medicare plans. When people are older, their needs tend to change a little faster, so there is this flexible period each year to move from one plan to another if needed.
 Aside from monthly premiums, what factors should people consider when choosing health insurance?  People at different ages and different states of health require different levels of coverage. It’s important to consider how much financial risk you want to take on. That includes looking at premiums, co-pays and deductibles.
 Valeriya 
 People should also see whether a doctor, hospital or clinic they use is in each plan’s network. When you ask your doctor, make sure you ask if they are specifically “in network” for your health plan. Many doctors and medical facilities will say they accept a certain insurance, but they may be out of your network, which can raise your costs dramatically. If you’re considering a Louisiana Blue plan, you can visit lablue.com to see which providers are in the plan’s network. If you already have a Louisiana Blue plan, you can check the MyLaBlue app [available at lablue.com , as a mobile app or linked through an existing MyChart account] to see which providers are in the network for your plan.
 How can an agent help people navigate their options?  Buying a health insurance product can be confusing. Sometimes there are lots of choices. Agents can be most helpful in this process. They may ask your age, health considerations, medications and which doctors you want to use to help you zero in on the plan that is best for you. They will use your ZIP code and income level to see what plans are available to you and estimate your out-of-pocket costs. They are the experts at taking all of those considerations into account, walking you through your options and discussing the pros and cons of each one.
 HealthCare.gov in particular can be daunting. Our recent Straight Talk blog explains the dangers of searching online for plans. Many online search results unfortunately lead people to misinformation, high-pressure tactics and even fraud. Agents know what is legitimate and what is not.
 What should people know about HealthCare.gov plans with federal subsidies?  When you apply for a policy that includes federal assistance, you are responsible for providing your income estimate for next year. If you misjudge that estimate and receive too much assistance, the IRS will want most or even all of it back when you file your taxes. In the past there were limits on how much of that money the government would claw back.  That has changed this year. The limits are gone. There’s much more risk in making that estimate because the penalties could be much more substantial now.
 This is another situation where using an agent is helpful. They are integral in making sure your income estimates are conservative and sensible. It’s never been more important to have an agent involved who understands what the government will expect and what the consequences of an error could be.
 And, if you enter your income information and qualify for the state Medicaid program, HealthCare.gov will let you know that.
 How often should people change or review their health insurance plans?  If you have a plan that is working for you and nothing major has changed in your life, including your health, dependents or employment, it may be fine to stick with it. Still, it doesn’t hurt to look at your options each year. Plans come and go, and what you had before through your employer or HealthCare.gov may be different in the coming year.
 Olena Miroshnichenko 
 What are the main things people should do now, before choosing a health plan?  Look at your current coverage, the dependents you are covering and who you will be covering in 2027. For everyone on your plan, look at the medications they take, the doctors they see and the hospitals they use.
 If you have health insurance through your employer, make sure to know their policies around covering spouses. At many companies, if an employee is married, employers will ask if the spouse has access to health insurance at their own job. If they do, the spouse may either not be offered insurance at all, or there will be a substantial fee to cover them on your employer’s plan.
 Lastly, remember that you can’t predict everything. Unexpected events can and do happen. The best you can do is make sure you are covering the health needs you know about now.
 Call 1-800-821-2758 or visit lablue.com to connect with a licensed, experienced agent who can help you review your 2027 health plan options. There’s no obligation to buy, and you do not pay anything to work with an agent.
